title: Clarus the dogcow
hook: A spotted Mac doodle became Apple's dogcow, and her official sound is "Moof".
peek: Susan Kare drew a small spotted dog for an early Macintosh picture font. Apple later used it to show page orientation in printer settings, where people decided it looked like a cow too, and named her Clarus.
lede: In the early 1980s the designer Susan Kare drew a little spotted dog for Cairo, a Macintosh font made of pictures. Apple later put the image in the Page Setup dialog, where it flipped and turned to show how a page would print. Its long body and spots looked half dog, half cow, and Apple's engineers took the joke and ran with it.

bullets.text: Kare designed many of the original Mac icons and fonts, including the happy Mac and the trash can. Cairo was a font full of small pictures, and the dogcow began there simply as a dog.

Apple's developer support team gave her a name, Clarus, and her sound, "Moof", in a tongue-in-cheek technical note in the late 1980s. The name played on Claris, an Apple software company of the time. Clarus is officially a she.

The dogcow showed options like flipping a page or inverting its colours. She was dropped from Mac printing settings for years, then quietly returned in macOS Ventura in 2022, to the delight of longtime fans.
